outputs.L3: This text reviews recent advances in the operator-algebraic approach to conformal quantum field theory, with particular emphasis on the role of representation theory in classification. outputs.L4:
Recent advances in the operator-algebraic approach to conformal quantum field theory have shown that representation theory provides one of the most effective tools for understanding and classifying conformal models. In this framework, a conformal quantum field theory is described by a conformal net: a family of von Neumann algebras associated with intervals of the circle and satisfying locality, covariance, isotony, and positivity of energy. This formulation makes it possible to study quantum fields through the structural properties of local operator algebras, without relying on a particular choice of generating fields or Lagrangian description.

A central problem is the classification of conformal nets and their local extensions. The representation theory of a net encodes its superselection sectors, fusion rules, statistics, and internal symmetries. For theories satisfying suitable finiteness conditions—most notably complete rationality—the representation category has the structure of a modular tensor category. This provides a powerful bridge between operator algebras, subfactor theory, tensor categories, and the representation theory of loop groups, affine Lie algebras, and vertex operator algebras.

Subfactor methods play an especially important role in this program. Inclusions of local algebras give rise to numerical and categorical invariants, while canonical endomorphisms and sector theory describe possible extensions of a given conformal net. Techniques such as induction of sectors allow representations of a subnet to be related to those of a larger theory. Locality imposes strong restrictions on the resulting extensions, converting the classification problem into a tractable analysis of algebraic objects within the relevant representation category.

These ideas have led to substantial progress in the study of rational conformal field theories. Once the irreducible representations and their fusion structure are known, one can investigate modular invariants, intermediate subnets, orbifolds, coset constructions, and local extensions. Representation theory therefore does more than describe the particle-like sectors of an already constructed theory: it can guide the construction of new models and, in favorable cases, determine all theories satisfying prescribed structural conditions.

Based on joint work with R. Longo, this perspective emphasizes that representation theory is not merely one component of the operator-algebraic approach but a central organizing principle for classification. The interplay among conformal nets, superselection sectors, modular tensor categories, and subfactors yields a rigorous framework in which both individual models and entire families of conformal quantum field theories can be analyzed. Recent results demonstrate that this framework is capable of turning broad classification questions into precise problems in operator algebras and categorical representation theory, thereby advancing the systematic classification of conformal quantum field theories.

**Classifying Conformal Quantum Field Theories through Representation Theory**

Drawing on joint work with Roberto Longo, this talk will describe how operator-algebraic representation theory can be used to classify conformal quantum field theories. In the framework of conformal nets, superselection sectors form braided tensor categories whose structure encodes fusion, statistics, and possible extensions of the theory. I will explain how finite-index subfactors, modularity, and representation-theoretic invariants lead to rigorous classification results, and illustrate the approach through examples of rational conformal field theories.

**Advances in Algebraic Conformal Quantum Field Theory**

I will review recent developments in algebraic conformal quantum field theory, emphasizing the classification of conformal nets through operator-algebraic and representation-theoretic methods. For completely rational nets, Doplicher–Haag–Roberts sectors form a modular tensor category, while inclusions and extensions of nets can be studied using subfactor theory, \(Q\)-systems, \(\alpha\)-induction, and modular invariants. These tools translate structural questions about local quantum field theories into tractable problems involving tensor categories and finite-index inclusions.

Particular attention will be given to a series of joint papers with R. Longo, including the classification of local conformal nets with central charge \(c<1\), the analysis of their extensions and two-dimensional counterparts, and the role of modular invariance in establishing completeness results. I will also discuss how these methods clarify the relation between conformal nets, vertex operator algebras, and rational conformal field theory, and indicate current directions toward broader classification results.
